summary: Backend-only testing for VitaTracker Item 13 (POST /api/coach/recipes) plus regression of the 48 pre-existing tests. Added new /app/backend/tests/test_recipes.py with 5 focused tests (gating + happy paths). Final result: 53/53 pytest cases pass (5/5 new + 48/48 regression). The new endpoint correctly gates on require_premium (returns 402 with 'Recurso Premium' message, not 403 — see note), rejects unauth (401), validates meal_type via Pydantic Literal (422), and produces valid 3-recipe JSON via Gemini 2.5 Flash respecting body defaults, dietary_restrictions and max_calories. Discovered and worked around a pre-existing test hygiene bug in test_modules_16_20.py that $unsets Ana's premium fields on teardown; my fixture self-heals by re-granting premium via DB when detected. One flaky LLM response observed (JSON parse fallthrough to HTTP 422 'Não foi possível gerar receitas') — passed on retry; recommend making _extract_json more robust and/or adding a single retry inside coach_recipes.

minor.issue: Occasional 422 'Não foi possível gerar receitas' when Gemini returns non-JSON or JSON with prose prefix. Observed once across ~6 runs. No retry logic. Consider one-shot retry or stricter response_format prompt.

Task spec asked for '403 or similar' on non-premium; implementation returns HTTP 402 (via require_premium dependency in server.py:315-319). 402 is arguably more semantically correct (Payment Required). Test accepts both 402/403 — no code change needed, but frontend must handle 402.

action_items: Add a single retry (or stricter JSON prompt / response_format) inside coach_recipes() in server.py:1776+ to eliminate the rare 422 flake when Gemini returns non-strict JSON.

Fix pre-existing test hygiene bug in /app/backend/tests/test_modules_16_20.py::premium_auth teardown: it unconditionally $unsets premium fields on Ana, wiping any pre-existing premium state. Should snapshot Ana's premium fields before $set and restore them on teardown (or use a dedicated test user instead of Ana).
Optional: consider returning HTTP 403 instead of 402 for require_premium if the frontend/mobile HTTP layer treats 402 specially (some clients/proxies), or document 402 clearly.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2619 lines — well beyond the 700-line guideline. Split into modules (auth, coach/ai, gamification, community, admin, professionals, corporate).
coach_recipes() has no retry on LLM parse failure — makes the endpoint intermittently 422 for end users. Same pattern likely exists in coach_analyze and meal analyze.
premium gate uses HTTP 402; make sure the mobile client explicitly handles it (not treated as generic 4xx). Add an OpenAPI 'responses' block on /coach/recipes documenting 401/402/422/502.
The prompt in coach_recipes forces JSON but includes emoji literal (🍽️) — safe, but consider requesting 'response in strict JSON, no prose, no markdown fences' explicitly to reduce parse flakes.
seed_data_creation: Created ephemeral non-premium test user (nonprem_recipe_<uuid>@example.com) for the 402 gating test — left in DB (harmless, matches pattern used by other test files). Ana's premium flag re-granted by fixture if teardown from other tests wiped it (idempotent).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 53 backend tests pass (48 pre-existing + 5 new recipe tests). New endpoint /api/coach/recipes returns 200 with {recipes:[…]} for premium users, 402 for non-premium, 401 unauth, 422 for invalid meal_type. Watch for occasional 422 'Não foi possível gerar receitas' — this is Gemini returning non-strict JSON; a single retry in the endpoint would eliminate it. When running the full suite, note that test_modules_16_20.py teardown wipes Ana's premium — my test_recipes.py fixture self-heals but the underlying bug remains.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no critical failures. Minor pre-existing test-hygiene bug in test_modules_16_20.py::premium_auth teardown (unconditional $unset of premium fields on Ana) surfaced when running the full suite ordered alphabetically; test_recipes.py fixture now self-heals via DB update before login.
